title: pacifist — malaise

translations.translation: 和平主义者， 反战主义者

sentences.sentence: Many protesters insist they are pacifists, opposed to war in all forms.
sentences.translation: 许多抗议者坚持说他们是和平主义者，反对一切形式的战争。

sentences.sentence: People showed remarkable resilience during the war.
sentences.translation: 战争期间人们表现得特别坚韧。

sentences.sentence: That of course raised my ire.
sentences.translation: 这当然也引起我的忿怒。

sentences.sentence: We talk about the surface emotions, the ire or indifference, and blame the other.
sentences.translation: 我们讨论表面的情绪、忿怒或是漠不关心，并且责怪另一方。

sentences.sentence: I cannot change who I am, but going forward, I can temper my ire—and understand that we all navigate disputes differently.
sentences.translation: 我不能改变自己，但是向前看的话，我可以缓和我的愤怒——理解我们都需以不同的方式解决争端。

sentences.sentence: The rehearsal process also irked him increasingly.
sentences.translation: 排练过程也更加让他厌烦。

translations.translation: 无嗅的， 没有气味的

sentences.sentence: Install a CO detector to alert you of the presence of the deadly, odorless, colorless gas.
sentences.translation: 安装一氧化碳检测器来警告是否存在这种致命的、无色无味的气体。

sentences.sentence: Many smokeless, odorless incinerators for disposal of animal carcasses are available commercially.
sentences.translation: 市场上有许多种处理尸体的无烟、 无臭的焚尸炉出售。

sentences.sentence: Learning how to safely harness the invisible, odorless resource took some time. Many a building was blown to matchwood because of leaking gas. In 1908, a mattress factory exploded.
sentences.translation: 学习如何安全使用这种无形、无味的资源需要时间。很多建筑因为漏气而被炸成碎片。1908年，一家床垫厂发生爆炸。

sentences.sentence: Lefèvre’s comments unleashed a wave of protest.
sentences.translation: 勒菲弗的评论引发了一波抗议的浪潮。

translations.translation: 摇摇欲坠； 步履蹒跚

sentences.sentence: Lorrimer swayed a little, tottered, and fell.
sentences.translation: 洛里默身体微微摇晃，蹒跚几步后跌倒在地。

sentences.sentence: However, the rationale for such initiatives is not, of course, solely economic.
sentences.translation: 但是，这些积极行动的根本原因当然不全是出于经济目的。

sentences.sentence: Childcare was seen as women’s work, and men disdained it.
sentences.translation: 照看儿童被视为女人做的工作，男人对此很不屑。

translations.translation: 强迫， 强制； 施恩惠于…

sentences.sentence: The storm got worse and worse. Finally, I was obliged to abandon the car and continue on foot.
sentences.translation: 暴风雨越来越猛烈。最终，我被迫弃车徒步前行。

sentences.sentence: an overt attempt to silence their political opponents
sentences.translation: 他们想压制政敌言论的明显企图

sentences.sentence: Overt race discrimination is illegal.
sentences.translation: 公然的种族歧视是非法的。

translations.translation: 很快地； 紧紧地； 深沉地

phrases.translation: 夏令时间；日光节约时间（daylight-saving time）

sentences.sentence: Slow down – you’re driving too fast.
sentences.translation: 慢点——你开得太快了。

sentences.sentence: a fast-moving river
sentences.translation: 湍急的河流

sentences.sentence: Johnny ran off as fast as his legs could carry him (= running as quickly as he could ) .
sentences.translation: 约翰尼飞也似的跑开了。

phrases.translation: 光栅常量；晶格恒量；点阵常数
光栅光谱仪，光栅分光计

sentences.sentence: a harsh grating voice
sentences.translation: 刺耳难听的声音

sentences.sentence: the turbulent times of the French Revolution
sentences.translation: 法国大革命的动荡时期

sentences.sentence: He has had a turbulent political career.
sentences.translation: 他的政治生涯动荡不定。

sentences.sentence: The Obama administration and police officers around the country say no, and their precedent is the past.
sentences.translation: 奥巴马政府和全国各地的警官说不可以，他们引为依据的先例就是“过去”。

sentences.sentence: There is no historical precedent that can tell us what happens to established democracies when most citizens go years, even decades, without an improvement in their standard of living.
sentences.translation: 没有历史先例能告诉我们，当大多数人民的生活水平在几年、甚至几十年间维持不变时，一个已经确立根基的民主国家会发生什么。

sentences.sentence: An east London school has set a precedent by fining pupils who break the rules.
sentences.translation: 伦敦东区的一所学校开创了对违反校规的学生处以罚金的先例。

sentences.sentence: the dappled shade of the trees
sentences.translation: 斑驳的树影

translations.translation: 要塞； 堡垒， 根据地

sentences.sentence: The fighters moved south to their mountain stronghold.
sentences.translation: 战士们向南行进，到达他们在山上的据点。

sentences.sentence: Pilcher’s books have humour, good characterization, and lively dialogue.
sentences.translation: 皮尔彻的书风趣幽默，人物塑造到位，而且对话生动。

sentences.sentence: Their head office was an imposing edifice.
sentences.translation: 他们的总部大楼是一幢宏伟建筑。

sentences.sentence: He complained of depression, headaches, and malaise.
sentences.translation: 他说他有情绪低落、头痛和不安的症状。

text:
英语词汇 · GRE · 第 485 单元

pacifist
音标：英 /'pæsɪfɪst/  美 /'pæsɪfɪst/
n.  和平主义者， 反战主义者
例句：Many protesters insist they are pacifists, opposed to war in all forms.
许多抗议者坚持说他们是和平主义者，反对一切形式的战争。

resilience
音标：英 /rɪ'zɪliəns/  美 /rɪˈzɪliəns/
n.  恢复力， 弹力
短语：modulus of resilience — [力]回弹模量
例句：People showed remarkable resilience during the war.
战争期间人们表现得特别坚韧。

ire
音标：英 /'aɪər/  美 /'aɪɚ/
v.  激怒
n. 愤怒
例句：That of course raised my ire.
这当然也引起我的忿怒。
例句：We talk about the surface emotions, the ire or indifference, and blame the other.
我们讨论表面的情绪、忿怒或是漠不关心，并且责怪另一方。
例句：I cannot change who I am, but going forward, I can temper my ire—and understand that we all navigate disputes differently.
我不能改变自己，但是向前看的话，我可以缓和我的愤怒——理解我们都需以不同的方式解决争端。

irk
音标：英 /ɜːrk/  美 /ɝk/
v.  使苦恼， 使厌烦
例句：The rehearsal process also irked him increasingly.
排练过程也更加让他厌烦。

odorless
音标：英 /'oudərləs/
adj.  无嗅的， 没有气味的
例句：Install a CO detector to alert you of the presence of the deadly, odorless, colorless gas.
安装一氧化碳检测器来警告是否存在这种致命的、无色无味的气体。
例句：Many smokeless, odorless incinerators for disposal of animal carcasses are available commercially.
市场上有许多种处理尸体的无烟、 无臭的焚尸炉出售。
例句：Learning how to safely harness the invisible, odorless resource took some time. Many a building was blown to matchwood because of leaking gas. In 1908, a mattress factory exploded.
学习如何安全使用这种无形、无味的资源需要时间。很多建筑因为漏气而被炸成碎片。1908年，一家床垫厂发生爆炸。

unleash
音标：英 /ʌn'liːʃ/  美 /ʌnˈliʃ/
v.  发泄， 释放
例句：Lefèvre’s comments unleashed a wave of protest.
勒菲弗的评论引发了一波抗议的浪潮。

totter
音标：英 /'tɑːtər/  美 /'tɑtɚ/
v.  摇摇欲坠； 步履蹒跚
例句：Lorrimer swayed a little, tottered, and fell.
洛里默身体微微摇晃，蹒跚几步后跌倒在地。

rationale
音标：英 /ˌræʃə'næl/  美 /,ræʃə'næl/
n.  基本原理
例句：However, the rationale for such initiatives is not, of course, solely economic.
但是，这些积极行动的根本原因当然不全是出于经济目的。

disdain
音标：英 /dɪs'deɪn/  美 /dɪs'den/
v. 轻视，鄙视
n.  轻视， 鄙视
例句：Childcare was seen as women’s work, and men disdained it.
照看儿童被视为女人做的工作，男人对此很不屑。

oblige
音标：英 /ə'blaɪdʒ/  美 /ə'blaɪdʒ/
v.  强迫， 强制； 施恩惠于…
例句：The storm got worse and worse. Finally, I was obliged to abandon the car and continue on foot.
暴风雨越来越猛烈。最终，我被迫弃车徒步前行。

overt
音标：英 /ou'vɜːrt/  美 /o'vɝt/
adj.  公开的， 非秘密的
例句：an overt attempt to silence their political opponents
他们想压制政敌言论的明显企图
例句：Overt race discrimination is illegal.
公然的种族歧视是非法的。

fast
音标：英 /fæst/  美 /fæst/
adv.  很快地； 紧紧地； 深沉地
n. 禁食，斋戒
短语：fast food — 速食，快餐
短语：as fast as — 和…一样快
短语：fast growth — 快速生长
短语：fast response — 快速响应
短语：fast algorithm — 快速算法
短语：fast fourier transform — 快速傅里叶变换
短语：hold fast — v. 紧紧抓住
短语：stand fast — 不让步；不后退
短语：fast moving — adj. 快速移动的
短语：fast track — 快速立法；快速通道
短语：fast and furious — 飞快地
短语：fast food restaurant — 速食店
短语：fast asleep — 熟睡的；很快地入睡
短语：fast lane — 快车道
短语：hard and fast — 严格的；固定不变的
短语：fast ethernet — 快速以太网
短语：fast reaction — 快速反应；快速核反应
短语：fast time — 夏令时间；日光节约时间（daylight-saving time）
短语：fast dry — 快干
短语：fast train — 快车
例句：Slow down – you’re driving too fast.
慢点——你开得太快了。
例句：a fast-moving river
湍急的河流
例句：Johnny ran off as fast as his legs could carry him (= running as quickly as he could ) .
约翰尼飞也似的跑开了。

grating
音标：英 /'greɪtɪŋ/  美 /'gretɪŋ/
adj.  刺耳的； 恼人的
短语：fiber grating — 光纤光栅
短语：diffraction grating — 衍射光栅；绕射光栅
短语：holographic grating — [化]全息照相栅
短语：concave grating — 凹面光栅
短语：grating constant — 光栅常量；晶格恒量；点阵常数
短语：grating monochromator — 光栅单色仪
短语：transmission grating — 透射光栅
短语：grating spectrometer — 光栅光谱仪，光栅分光计
短语：grating spectrograph — 光栅摄谱仪
短语：reflection grating — 反射光栅
短语：plane grating — 平面光栅
例句：a harsh grating voice
刺耳难听的声音

turbulent
音标：英 /'tɜːrbjələnt/  美 /'tɝbjələnt/
adj.  混乱的； 骚乱的
短语：turbulent flow — 湍流；紊流
短语：turbulent boundary layer — 湍流边界层；紊两面层
短语：turbulent diffusion — 湍流扩散
短语：turbulent current — 湍流；紊流
短语：turbulent fluctuation — n. 紊流脉动；紊动
短语：turbulent fluid — 湍流；紊流
短语：turbulent motion — [物]涡（旋运）动；湍动
例句：the turbulent times of the French Revolution
法国大革命的动荡时期
例句：He has had a turbulent political career.
他的政治生涯动荡不定。

precedent
音标：英 /'presɪdənt/  美 /'prɛsɪdənt/
adj. 在先的，在前的
n.  先例； 判例
短语：judicial precedent — 司法判例
短语：condition precedent — 先决条件
短语：conditions precedent — 先决条件
例句：The Obama administration and police officers around the country say no, and their precedent is the past.
奥巴马政府和全国各地的警官说不可以，他们引为依据的先例就是“过去”。
例句：There is no historical precedent that can tell us what happens to established democracies when most citizens go years, even decades, without an improvement in their standard of living.
没有历史先例能告诉我们，当大多数人民的生活水平在几年、甚至几十年间维持不变时，一个已经确立根基的民主国家会发生什么。
例句：An east London school has set a precedent by fining pupils who break the rules.
伦敦东区的一所学校开创了对违反校规的学生处以罚金的先例。

dappled
音标：英 /'dæpld/  美 /'dæpld/
adj.  有斑点的， 斑驳的
例句：the dappled shade of the trees
斑驳的树影

stronghold
音标：英 /'strɔːŋhould/  美 /'strɔŋhold/
n.  要塞； 堡垒， 根据地
例句：The fighters moved south to their mountain stronghold.
战士们向南行进，到达他们在山上的据点。

characterization
音标：英 /ˌkærəktəraɪ'zeɪʃn/  美 /,kærəktəraɪ'zeʃən/
n.  描绘， 刻画
短语：material characterization — 材料特性表达
例句：Pilcher’s books have humour, good characterization, and lively dialogue.
皮尔彻的书风趣幽默，人物塑造到位，而且对话生动。

edifice
音标：英 /'edɪfɪs/  美 /'ɛdɪfɪs/
n.  宏伟的建筑
例句：Their head office was an imposing edifice.
他们的总部大楼是一幢宏伟建筑。

malaise
音标：英 /mə'leɪz/  美 /mə'lez/
n.  不适， 不舒服
短语：general malaise — 全身不适
例句：He complained of depression, headaches, and malaise.
他说他有情绪低落、头痛和不安的症状。
